messages:
Anya (PM): Kicking off a short thread — proposal for a hardware-aware localization onboarding window. TL;DR: batch onboarding by GPU family + data-residency week to reduce benchmarking variance and infra churn.

Carl (Infra): +1. We should tie this to Dedicated pool reservations so customers on reserved capacity aren't impacted.

Maria (Eng-ML): Important: A100 vs H100 have different perf curves. Bench configs must include seq-length buckets and KV-cache hit-rate samples.

Sam (ProdOps): Suggest adding a soft manifest flag `prefer-h100` so the rollout tool can schedule canaries into the right pool.

Leo (Solutions): Customer ask: EU-only onboarding windows for privacy-sensitive pilots. Can we align those with region maintenance windows? :thinking_face:

Anya (PM): Proposed high-level schedule snippet: 
```
- eu-local-week: 2026-05-10 -> 2026-05-16 (A100 pool reserved, EU region)
- global-speed-week: 2026-05-24 -> 2026-05-30 (H100 pool reserved, global)
```
Goals: reduce cross-hardware variance, allow customer canaries inside a controlled window, and give eng a 48h stabilization buffer before general catalog exposure.

Maria (Eng-ML): Bench matrix suggestion: sample slices = short chat (0-128 tokens), doc-gen (0-1024 tokens), embeddings stress; metrics = p95 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, and a quality proxy (BLEU/perplexity delta on eval set).

Carl (Infra): Ops note: we need autoscaler policy tweaks — recommend disabling "startup-burst" during reserved windows to keep noise low. Also reserve capacity tags so scheduling is deterministic.

onboard-bot: Template created: hw-localization-2026-v1, owners assigned: @Anya (PM), @Maria (Eng-ML).

Sam (ProdOps): Question: how do migrations/pinning interact with windows? If a customer is pinned to an older model, do we force migration into a later window or allow immediate opt-in? Need ticket flow.

Anya (PM): Proposal for pin/migration policy: default = schedule migrations to the next matching hardware window. Customers can request immediate migration via support ticket; add `migration-delay` tag with allowed max 90 days.

Leo (Solutions): Also require a compact compatibility checklist per model: api-compat, tokenizer parity, response-shape tests, and a short migration notes section for customers.

Maria (Eng-ML): Add a quantitative quality gate: run a 5% traffic A/B holdback for 7 days; quality delta must be < 2% on our eval slice (or we fail and rollback).

Carl (Infra): Fallback policy question: if reserved pool saturates mid-window, route to compatible variant on other family with `degraded-perf` flag and trigger alert to #eng-oncall. We should document expected perf delta thresholds.

Anya (PM): Next steps (owners & deadlines): finalize schedule by EOD Friday (Anya), bench matrix and eval harness (Maria), infra policy + autoscaler prototype (Carl), support ticket template & migration flow (Sam), customer comm & FAQ (Leo). If no objections I'll draft the runbook.

Maria (Eng-ML): I'll open a PR with the eval harness and link it in the runbook draft.

Leo (Solutions): I'll assemble a 1-pager FAQ for enterprise customers explaining windows, pinning choices, and opt-in flow.

Sam (ProdOps): +1 — I'll create the migration ticket template and add tagging conventions.

Carl (Infra): Will prototype the autoscaler tweak in staging and post a short log + perf snapshot by Wednesday.

Anya (PM): Great. Thanks everyone — spinning up the runbook now. :thumbsup:
